newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli CPI-linked bonds end sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Israeli CPI-linked bonds end sharply lower.

text.p: Israeli inflation-linked bonds fell sharply on Sunday, as investors bailed out in favour of unlinked bonds, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.33 pct to 168.19
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.16 pct at 159.49
Overall, bond prices closed mixed, as unlinked bonds rose and dollar-linked bonds held steady. Volume was moderate at 110 million shekels, traders said.

"Inflation-linked bonds fell sharply after the Bank of Israel said on Thursday it would resume issuing linked bonds after a lapse of several months," said Roy Meir at Simodan, adding: "They will continue to decline in the coming days."
CPI-linked long bonds declined for the second consecutive session after a sharp rise during the last two months, said Michael Weiss at Evergreen Capital Markets.
Traders bailing out of CPI bonds bought unlinked bonds, pushing their prices higher. Makams also closed higher, but yields were almost unchanged at about 15.3 percent, said Meir.
"Investors are showing a preference for unlinked bonds because they expect that inflation will be relatively low while interest rates remain high," Weiss said.
Meir said dollar-linked bonds were stable in thin trading. "Investors are waiting to see where the dollar is going," he said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
